name: Pressure in solids liquids and gases

questions.q: What is the scientific definition of pressure?
a: Force acting normally per unit area
Total mass divided by total volume
Speed multiplied by time
Energy transferred per second

questions.q: What are the standard SI units for pressure?
a: Newtons (N)
Pascals (Pa) or N/m squared
Joules per second (W)
Kilograms per cubic metre

questions.q: Why do snowshoes prevent a person from sinking deeply into soft snow?
a: They reduce the person's total weight
They increase the surface area, decreasing the pressure exerted on the snow
They increase the downward force on the ground
They trap air beneath the feet to create heat

questions.q: Why is the cutting edge of a knife made very thin?
a: To make the knife look nicer
To increase the total mass of the blade
To reduce the friction against food
To provide a very small surface area, which concentrates the force and creates high pressure for cutting

questions.q: How does pressure change as you go deeper underwater?
a: Pressure increases because of the weight of the water above
Pressure decreases because the temperature drops
Pressure stays exactly the same
Pressure drops to zero immediately

questions.q: What causes gas pressure inside a closed container?
a: Chemical reactions between the container walls
Collisions of fast-moving gas particles with the container walls
Gravity pulling gas molecules downward
Magnetic forces between air atoms

questions.q: Which of the following statements about liquid pressure is correct?
a: Liquid pressure acts only in a downward direction
Liquid pressure decreases with depth
Liquid pressure acts equally in all directions at a given depth
Liquid pressure depends on the color of the liquid

questions.q: What happens to atmospheric pressure as you climb higher up a mountain?
a: Atmospheric pressure increases rapidly
Atmospheric pressure fluctuates wildly
Atmospheric pressure stays constant
Atmospheric pressure decreases because there is less air above you

questions.q: If a box weighing 200 N rests on a surface with an area of 2 square metres, what pressure does it exert?
a: 100 Pascals
400 Pascals
0.01 Pascals
198 Pascals

questions.q: Why do deep-sea divers need special reinforced diving suits or submersibles?
a: To keep them warm in the dark
To withstand the immense water pressure at great depths
To help them swim much faster
To increase their overall body weight

questions.q: What happens to the pressure of a fixed mass of gas inside a syringe if its volume is compressed (decreased) at a constant temperature?
a: The pressure decreases to zero
The pressure remains unchanged
The pressure increases because particles collide more frequently with the walls
The pressure drops by half

questions.q: Why do sharp drawing pins have a large flat head on one end and a sharp point on the other?
a: To make them easier to paint
To ensure they roll away easily
To prevent them from bending in half
To allow a large thumb area to experience low pressure while the sharp point exerts high pressure to pierce wood

questions.q: Which scientific instrument is commonly used to measure atmospheric pressure?
a: A barometer
An ammeter
A thermometer
A newton meter

questions.q: What happens when you suck through a drinking straw to drink juice?
a: You pump juice upward using muscle power
You reduce the air pressure inside the straw, allowing higher atmospheric pressure on the liquid surface to push juice up
You create a magnetic field that attracts the liquid
You heat the liquid until it expands upward

questions.q: Why are dams built with much thicker walls at the bottom than at the top?
a: To save building materials near the surface
To look more symmetrical
To withstand the much greater water pressure found at greater depths
To prevent fish from swimming too low

questions.q: What is atmospheric pressure at sea level approximately equal to?
a: 1 Pascal
10 Pascals
1,000 Pascals
100,000 Pascals (or 100 kPa)

questions.q: How does increasing the temperature of a sealed container of gas affect its pressure?
a: Pressure increases because particles gain kinetic energy and collide harder and faster with the walls
Pressure decreases because particles slow down
Pressure stays the same because mass does not change
Pressure drops to zero immediately

questions.q: Why do heavy trucks have many more wheels than standard cars?
a: To use up more fuel
To distribute the heavy load over a larger surface area, reducing the pressure on the road surface
To travel much faster on highways
To make steering easier for the driver

questions.q: What term describes an upward force exerted by a fluid on an object placed in it?
a: Gravitational pull
Frictional drag
Upthrust (buoyancy)
Magnetic repulsion

questions.q: Why does a solid steel ball sink in water, whereas a massive steel ship floats?
a: Steel is lighter than water
The ship is made of hollow sections containing air, displacing a large volume of water and creating enough upthrust
The ship has a motor pushing it up
Water avoids solid balls

questions.q: If you double the force acting on a surface while keeping the contact area constant, what happens to the pressure?
a: The pressure is doubled
The pressure is halved
The pressure remains unchanged
The pressure drops to zero

questions.q: What causes a suction cup to stick firmly to a smooth wall?
a: Glue inside the rubber cup
Air is pressed out from underneath, creating a low-pressure zone so higher outside atmospheric pressure pushes it against the wall
Magnetic attraction between rubber and wall
Electrostatic charge generated by rubbing

questions.q: Which of the following factors does NOT affect the pressure at a certain depth in a liquid?
a: The depth below the liquid surface
The density of the liquid
The shape of the container holding the liquid
The acceleration due to gravity

questions.q: What happens to a sealed bag of crisps (chips) if you take it from sea level up to the top of a high mountain?
a: It shrinks into a flat wrapper
It dissolves into air
It remains completely unchanged
It swells up and expands because outside atmospheric pressure is lower than the pressure inside the bag

questions.q: Why are high-altitude aircraft cabins pressurized?
a: To ensure passengers and crew have enough air pressure to breathe comfortably
To make the airplane fly faster
To prevent the wings from melting
To save electrical power

questions.q: What happens to the volume of a gas bubble as it rises from the deep bottom of a lake to the surface?
a: The bubble shrinks to a tiny speck
The bubble expands in size because the surrounding water pressure decreases
The bubble turns into a solid crystal
The bubble disappears instantly

questions.q: Why do camels have broad, wide feet instead of narrow hooves?
a: To help them run faster on rocks
To dig deeper wells in sand
To distribute their body weight over a large area, preventing them from sinking into soft sand
To keep their legs cool in the sun

questions.q: What happens when a balloon is filled with a gas and heated with a hair dryer?
a: The gas particles slow down
The balloon shrinks in size
The gas pressure drops to zero
The gas expands, increasing pressure or volume, making the balloon rise if it is lighter than air

questions.q: If a force of 500 N is applied over a surface area of 10 square metres, what is the pressure?
a: 50 Pascals
5,000 Pascals
0.02 Pascals
490 Pascals

questions.q: Why does a helium-filled weather balloon expand as it ascends higher into the atmosphere?
a: The temperature inside increases rapidly
External atmospheric pressure decreases with altitude, allowing the internal gas pressure to expand the balloon
Helium turns into a solid
Gravity pulls the balloon outward

questions.q: Which state of matter transmits pressure equally in all directions within a closed system, as described by Pascal's principle?
a: Solid blocks
Rigid metals
Enclosed fluids (liquids and gases)
Gaseous plasmas only

questions.q: Why are stiletto heels more likely to damage wooden floors than flat shoes worn by a person of the same weight?
a: Stiletto heels are made of steel
The person walks faster in heels
Heels absorb moisture from the floor
The very small contact area of the heel concentrates the force, creating extremely high pressure

questions.q: What causes an object to float in water according to Archimedes' principle?
a: The upward upthrust force equals the downward weight of the object
The object has zero mass
Water pushes objects away magnetically
Gravity stops working underwater

questions.q: How does hydraulic machinery (such as car brakes or garage lifts) use liquid pressure?
a: To create infinite energy from nothing
To transmit force equally through an enclosed liquid from a small piston to a larger piston
To cool down engine parts
To remove friction completely

questions.q: Why is it difficult to breathe easily when climbing extremely high mountains like Mount Everest?
a: The air temperature is too warm
There is no oxygen present on mountains
Atmospheric pressure is lower, meaning fewer air molecules are packed into each breath
Gravity pulls air upward away from lungs

questions.q: What happens when you press a plunger down on a sealed bicycle pump?
a: The air inside vanishes
The temperature inside drops to freezing
The air molecules are destroyed
The volume of air decreases and the pressure increases, forcing air through the valve

questions.q: Which of these everyday objects is designed to produce a very high pressure by having a tiny surface area at its tip?
a: A sewing needle or drawing pin
A wooden baseball bat
A large foam mattress
A wide snow shovel

questions.q: Why do submarines have strong, thick steel hulls?
a: To make them invisible to radar
To withstand the immense crushing water pressure when submerged at deep levels
To make them float on the surface
To generate electrical power

questions.q: What happens to the pressure at the bottom of a container if you pour twice as much water into it?
a: The pressure drops by half
The pressure remains completely unchanged
The pressure doubles because the depth (and weight of water) doubles
The pressure increases a thousand times

questions.q: Why do ears sometimes 'pop' when an airplane ascends or descends rapidly?
a: Sound waves echo in the cabin
The engines change frequency
Headphones create static electricity
Air pressure inside the middle ear adjusts to match the changing external atmospheric pressure
